syllabusTopics: Biomolecules: Introduction and functions of carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, minerals, enzymes and water
Cell: Introduction of cell, concepts of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells

Detail structure of eukaryotic cells: cell wall, cell membrane, mitochondria, plastids, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi bodies, lysosomes, ribosomes, nucleus, chromosomes, cilia, flagella and cell inclusions
Cell division: Concept of cell cycle, types of cell division (amitosis, mitosis and meiosis) and significances

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The internal architecture of a eukaryotic cell is defined by membrane-bound organelles. Each has a specialised role: the plasma membrane controls transport; mitochondria and chloroplasts convert energy; RER/SER synthesise proteins and lipids; the Golgi, lysosomes and vacuoles process and store material; the nucleus controls inheritance; cilia, flagella and inclusions complete the picture.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Fluid-mosaic model: phospholipid bilayer + protein mosaic + cholesterol + glycocalyx
9+9 axonemal structure of cilia/flagella (9 doublets + central pair)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The cell wall is fully permeable; the plasma membrane is selectively permeable.  ·  RER is rough because of ribosomes; it makes PROTEINS. SER makes LIPIDS and detoxifies — it has no ribosomes.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB written answers expect a labelled organelle diagram plus a one-line function per organelle.  ·  The endosymbiotic theory (Mitochondria/chloroplast from engulfed prokaryotes) is a favourite 4-mark question.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Oxidative phosphorylation in the mitochondrial cristae produces the bulk of ATP.  ·  Secretory cells (e.g. pancreatic) have abundant RER and Golgi for protein export.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The Golgi packages proteins and lipids; it does not synthesise them.  ·  Lysosomes digest the cell's own material when damaged (autophagy); they are not plant cells' organelles (plants use vacuoles).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label a plant cell (all organelles)  ·  Draw the fluid-mosaic model

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: POWER: P=power (mitochondrion), O=oil & lipid (SER), W=wall (plant), E=envelope, R=respiration, power house = mitochondrion.  ·  MITOCHONDRIUM = MITOchondria make ENERGY (powerhouse).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Why are the mitochondria and chloroplast called "semi-autonomous" organelles?  ·  Differentiate rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Organelle label-and-function questions are very common.  ·  Draw the fluid-mosaic model with a labelled membrane.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Fluid-mosaic model  ·  Rough vs smooth ER  ·  Golgi functions  ·  Lysosomes/autophagy

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Each organelle has a distinct, frequently-examined function (mitochondrion→ATP, chloroplast→photosynthesis).  ·  RER makes protein; SER makes lipid; Golgi packages; lysosome digests.  ·  Plasma membrane is selectively permeable fluid mosaic.  ·  Nucleus + nucleolus + chromatin = genetic control; chromatin condenses into chromosomes.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own DNA and 70S ribosomes, suggesting an endosymbiotic origin.  ·  A single human liver cell may contain over one million ribosomes.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Describe the functions of the Golgi body in a plant cell.  ·  What is the significance of cristae in mitochondria?  ·  State the role of the nucleolus.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Explain endosymbiotic theory with evidence (own DNA, 70S ribosomes, double membrane).  ·  Compare plant and animal cells in a two-column table.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Central vacuole in a plant cell stores water, pigments and maintains turgor.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The "powerhouse of the cell" is: → B  ·  The fluid-mosaic model of the membrane was proposed by: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Cell wall (plant: cellulose; bacteria: peptidoglycan; fungi: chitin) — rigid, fully permeable outer support; in plants it can secondarily thicken (lignin).  ·  Plasma membrane: phospholipid bilayer + integral/protein (fluid-mosaic model, Singer & Nicolson 1972); selectively permeable; controls transport (diffusion, osmosis, active transport).  ·  Mitochondrion: site of aerobic respiration (Krebs + ETS → ATP); double membrane; cristae; "powerhouse of the cell".

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Nucleus & nucleolus  ·  9+9 axoneme  ·  Plant vs animal cells

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Endosymbiotic theory  ·  Plant-specific: cell wall, chloroplast, large central vacuole.  ·  Mitochondria and chloroplast carry their own DNA (endosymbiosis evidence).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Cilia and flagella both have a 9+9 microtubule axoneme; flagella are longer; in prokaryotes the flagellum has a different (no microtubule) structure.  ·  Chromatin (diffuse, interphase) and chromosomes (condensed, division) are the SAME genetic material in two forms.  ·  Contrast plant vs animal cells (wall, chloroplast, large vacuole vs centrioles).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Memorise organelle → function pairs (mitochondrion→ATP, ER→synthesis, Golgi→packaging, lysosome→digestion).  ·  Draw a plant cell with all labels in one pass.  ·  Learn the 9+9 axonemal structure of cilia and flagella.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Note plant-specific organelles (cell wall, chloroplast, central vacuole).  ·  The plasma membrane is the selectively permeable boundary of every cell.  ·  Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration; chloroplasts of photosynthesis.
